direction: Use the static score-based merge ordering (score_merge_static) to prioritize route pairs whose merge yields the smallest added distance, and keep the parallel merge schedule fixed rather than adaptive, so the 500 ms budget is spent on evaluating high-quality candidate merges.

operations.mechanism: Round 1 with no archive feedback or prior summary. Only cvrp_parallel_merge_static is allowed and postprocess must be none. The L2a static merge with score_merge_static is the sole available configuration, so the plan tests its core mechanism (static score-based merge prioritization) as the baseline direction; subsequent rounds can compare scalar scores to adjust merge granularity or tie-breaking.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: Ranking candidate route merges by the static merge score before executing the parallel merge will produce lower total CVRP distance than unranked/naive merging, because costly merges are deferred and cheap feasible merges are applied first.
